page: Amazon Web Services c9g.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by custom 64-bit ARMv9 AWS Graviton architecture with Neoverse-V3 cores. Built on the Nitro hypervisor, the instance provisions 16 dedicated physical cores running at 3.3 GHz with a single execution thread per core. The processor subsystem integrates 64 KB L1 data cache and 2 MB L2 cache per core, backed by 48 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 32.0 GB, establishing a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio aligned with compute-focused workloads. The platform includes an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth interface, contains no discrete GPU accelerators, and provides no local NVMe storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistence.

Benchmark results highlight strong computational throughput and memory efficiency. The instance registers top-tier results in Geekbench single-core evaluation (2353.0) and text processing (3161.0), alongside strong multi-core scaling (19897.0). Data compression execution is particularly robust, marked by top-tier single-threaded gzip throughput (36.52 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (17.33 GB/sec), complemented by strong multi-threaded decompression rates reaching 256.09 GB/sec. Memory responsiveness is corroborated by top-tier PassMark memory scores (4296.88), while web throughput benchmarks demonstrate sustained static serving rates of 54.43 GB/sec.

The 1:2 memory-to-core density presents an architectural tradeoff, limiting effectiveness for memory-heavy databases or caching tiers with large in-memory working sets. Additionally, the lack of onboard storage demands reliance on external EBS volumes for disk I/O. However, the dedicated single-thread core topology prevents hyperthread resource contention, offering consistent compute efficiency for CPU-bound batch processing, CI/CD build farms, web serving clusters, and lightweight machine learning inference.
description: Amazon Web Services c9g.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance based on the 64-bit ARMv9 AWS Graviton architecture with Neoverse-V3 cores. Operating on the Nitro hypervisor, it features 16 dedicated physical cores clocked at 3.3 GHz, 32.0 GB of memory, and an 8 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance lacks local disk storage and GPU hardware, relying on external network volumes for persistent storage. Benchmark evaluation shows top-tier Geekbench single-core execution, text processing, and single-threaded gzip compression, alongside strong multi-core scalability and top-tier PassMark memory metrics. Static web serving throughput reaches 54.43 GB/sec, while LLM text generation performs efficiently on smaller models. With 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, c9g.4xlarge delivers cost-efficient, predictable CPU performance for compute-intensive batch jobs, CI/CD compilation, web server fleets, and lightweight inference workloads.
